note: Selective CRTH2/DP2 antagonists were positive in the allergen exposure chamber (QAV680, BI 671800; fevipiprant's chamber study was never reported), but the only member taken to field SAR trials, setipiprant, was dosed off an asthma bronchial-challenge study and failed its 630-patient Phase 3 after a positive Phase 2, a post hoc occupancy model later calling the dose borderline; none reached the market.
label: Allergic rhinitis (CRTH2)

engagement.note: First member chamber study: QAV680 dosed 10 days, TNSS and nasal-lavage eosinophils scored under controlled pollen exposure.
engagement.quote: This study will compare the effectiveness of QAV680 against placebo in treating the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis in an Environmental Exposure Chamber.
engagement.confidence_note: Registry record only; no results ever posted. The trial was reported only as an ERS 2014 congress abstract (Erpenbeck et al., Eur Respir J 2014;44:P4075), which is not an admissible tier.
engagement.judgement: Opens the chamber track at the earliest member use I could verify (Novartis, start 2008-09, n=44). Novartis ran two more chamber studies (QAV680 + cetirizine NCT01103050, 2010; fevipiprant/QAW039 + montelukast NCT01804400, 2012, n=188) with no results posted and no publication found on PubMed.

engagement.note: BI 671800 cut nasal eosinophils, IL-4/eotaxin and the TNSS AUC in 146 chamber-challenged SAR patients: the chamber's own readouts moved in dosed patients.
engagement.short: Chamber readouts moved in dosed patients
engagement.quote: Compared with placebo, BI 671800 significantly reduced nasal eosinophil values (P < .05 for all doses)
engagement.confidence_note: JACI paywalled; abstract only. Quote is the verbatim opening of a longer sentence.
engagement.reason: Chamber readouts moved in dosed patients
engagement.judgement: Scored as the house style scores a challenge chamber in engagement: the chamber readout is itself the dosed-patient readout, so there is no separate model number to compare and magnitude is null. Year is the online date (2013-12-18); print 2014.
engagement.magnitude_basis: chamber nasal eosinophils, cytokines and TNSS are themselves the dosed-patient readout; no separate model number to compare

engagement.model: Human whole-blood PGD2 eosinophil shape-change assay
engagement.note: Class compounds were ranked on blockade of PGD2-induced eosinophil shape change in human whole blood; no dosed-human comparison yet. Opens the BI 671800 track (Krug 2014 ex vivo); the compounds dosed were non-member Amira DP2 antagonists.
engagement.quote: The activities of the compounds were evaluated in a human DP2 binding assay and a human whole blood eosinophil shape change assay.
engagement.judgement: Opener is a class proxy (Amira tricyclic DP2 antagonists, not a member), allowed with product_in_model false. The members used the same assay: QAV680 (Sandham 2013, doi 10.1016/j.bmc.2013.08.025, 'inhibition of CRTh2 driven human eosinophil ... activation in vitro'), fevipiprant (Sykes 2016, doi 10.1124/mol.115.101832, whole-blood shape change), setipiprant (Krause 2016 weights potency 'based on an eosinophil shape change assay'). No peer-reviewed preclinical BI 671800 paper exists (PubMed 'BI 671800' returns only clinical papers).

engagement.model: Human whole-blood PGD2 eosinophil shape-change assay
engagement.note: BI 671800 blocked ex vivo PGD2-induced eosinophil shape change dose-dependently in chamber-challenged SAR patients, as the in vitro assay predicted.
engagement.short: Ex vivo shape change blocked dose-dependently
engagement.quote: induced a dose-related reduction in ex vivo prostaglandin D2-mediated eosinophil shape change
engagement.confidence_note: JACI paywalled; abstract only. Quote is a verbatim fragment of a 45-word sentence; no in vitro potency is placed beside the ex vivo result in the abstract.
engagement.reason: Ex vivo stimulus blockade held in patients
engagement.judgement: Direct readout: the same assay run on dosed patients' blood (ex vivo blockade of the PGD2 stimulus). Paired comparison: the model side named is the member QAV680's in vitro use of the assay (Sandham 2013) because BI 671800's own in vitro run is unpublished; product_in_model is true because the assay in Krug is literally BI 671800 in the assay. Magnitude direction_only: 'dose-related' with no number in the abstract.
engagement.magnitude_basis: dose-related inhibition of ex vivo shape change reported without a number; in vitro potency not quoted beside it

dose.note: Chamber dose-ranging (QAV680; BI 671800 50/200/400 mg b.i.d.; fevipiprant) never fed a field SAR trial of the same drug.
dose.short: Chamber doses never field-tested in SAR
dose.quote: This study will compare the effectiveness of QAV680 against placebo in treating the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis in an Environmental Exposure Chamber.
dose.confidence_note: Registry record only; no results posted.
dose.reason: Chamber regimens never field-tested in SAR
dose.judgement: Untested, not empty: the chamber picked BI 671800 200 mg b.i.d. (Krug 2014) and ran QAV680 and fevipiprant dose arms, but no chamber-tested member ever had a field SAR trial, and the one field-tested member (setipiprant) was never in the rhinitis chamber, so no chamber regimen was ever checked against the field.

dose.model: Bronchial allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (setipiprant proof-of-mechanism)
dose.note: The regimen setipiprant carried into SAR, 1000 mg b.i.d., came from a 5-day asthma allergen-challenge crossover in 18 men; no exposure target stated.
dose.short: 1000 mg b.i.d. set by asthma challenge
dose.quote: In this 3-centre, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, cross-over study, 18 allergic asthmatic males were randomized to setipiprant 1000 mg or matching placebo b.i.d. for 5 consecutive days.
dose.confidence_note: Clin Exp Allergy paywalled; abstract only. The challenge study predates the SAR trials (which it dose-selected) but its earliest public record I verified is the 2014 paper, so model_first_use_year is 2014.
dose.judgement: Separate track from the rhinitis chamber: a different system (bronchial LAR/FEV1 in asthmatics, model_kind cross_indication) making a different prediction (a regimen). Ratner 2017 states this is where the 1000 mg b.i.d. dose came from.

dose.model: Bronchial allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (setipiprant proof-of-mechanism)
dose.note: 1000 mg b.i.d. was given in both field trials, worked in Phase 2 (-0.15 DNSS, p=0.030), failed in Phase 3 (-0.02, p=0.652); programme dropped. Dose scores the regimen reached and tolerated (same); the Phase 3 failure counts once, in efficacy.
dose.quote: However, no therapeutic effects were observed for this dose versus placebo in the Phase 3 trial.
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (open access, PMC5379543). Phase 3 trough exposure was lower than Phase 2 on the same nominal regimen (median 1120 vs 1540-1920 ng/mL; 250 mg capsules replaced by 500 mg tablets), which a re-scorer could read as 'target not reached'.
dose.judgement: Dose scored on its own prediction: the challenge regimen, 1000 mg b.i.d., was dosed in 579 + 630 field patients and tolerated, so target reached and stated margin held: same. Whether that dose worked is the efficacy question, scored contra there once. Ratner states the comparison (the dose 'was selected ... based on findings from a Phase 2 proof-of-mechanism study') and calls the Phase 2/3 discrepancy 'not fully known', hence unresolved. Year stays 2017: the 2012-04-02 Actelion release (via RTTNews) reports only the efficacy miss, not the regimen dosed or its tolerability, which are first public in Ratner 2017; Diamant 2014 predates that, so not a retrodiction.
dose.magnitude_basis: same regimen (1000 mg b.i.d.) in the challenge study and both field trials; the failure is the efficacy failure counted once

dose.model: PK/PD model of CRTH2 internalisation blockade (in silico occupancy target)
dose.note: Actelion's population PK/PD model set 90% blockade of PGD2-induced CRTH2 internalisation at trough as the dose target for setipiprant and ACT-453859.
dose.quote: Ninety percent of maximum blockade of CRTH2 internalization at trough is suggested as a quantitative PD target in clinical studies.
dose.confidence_note: Clin Pharmacokinet paywalled; abstract only. Online 2015-12-23, print 2016.
dose.judgement: Separate track: an in silico occupancy model is a different system from either human challenge and predicts a different quantity. It was built on setipiprant and ACT-453859 clinical PK/PD data after the SAR Phase 3 had completed (2012-02), so any setipiprant comparison from it is a retrodiction; the opener itself carries retrodiction false because no comparison is made yet.

dose.model: PK/PD model of CRTH2 internalisation blockade (in silico occupancy target)
dose.note: Model put under 30% of subjects at >=90% trough blockade on 1000 mg b.i.d.; the Phase 3 at that dose was null, as it implies. Retrodiction under the dose rule: built on setipiprant's own clinical PK/PD after its Phase 3 miss (public 2012-04-02).
dose.short: Occupancy model reproduces the Phase 3 null
dose.quote: the median percentage of subjects with at least 90% CRTH2 blockage at trough plasma setipiprant concentrations was higher with 1000 mg b.i.d. than with 500 mg b.i.d. doses, but still remained below 30%
dose.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). Quote is a verbatim fragment of a longer sentence. The model's number comes from Krause 2016 (abstract only); the side-by-side is Ratner's.
dose.reason: Retrodiction: dose below target, trial null
dose.judgement: Retro, never same: the model was built after the clinic knew the answer and Ratner invokes it post hoc ('it is possible that the 1000 mg b.i.d. dose of setipiprant provided borderline efficacy'). It reproduces the Phase 3 null but not the Phase 2 positive at the same dose, so source_calls_it is partial. No prospective test of the 90% target in rhinitis followed (ACT-453859 was not developed in SAR), so no later fresh entry.
dose.magnitude_basis: model: <30% of subjects at >=90% trough CRTH2 blockade on 1000 mg b.i.d.; trial: no effect on DNSS at that dose (-0.02, p=0.652); no common quantity

efficacy.note: First member chamber study: QAV680 dosed 10 days, TNSS scored over the last 2 h of pollen exposure on day 10.
efficacy.quote: This study will compare the effectiveness of QAV680 against placebo in treating the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis in an Environmental Exposure Chamber.
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record only; no results posted; reported only as an ERS 2014 congress abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Opens the chamber track at the earliest member use verified. The 2012-2013 fevipiprant chamber study (NCT01804400, n=188) has no posted results and no publication, so fevipiprant contributes nothing scorable.

efficacy.note: Chamber said CRTH2 antagonism relieves SAR symptoms (OC000459, Horak 2012; BI 671800 TNSS AUC -17%), but setipiprant's field Phase 3 (miss public 2012-04-02) found none. Retrodiction: chamber result public after that miss; it failed to reproduce it.
efficacy.short: Chamber said yes; field Phase 3 null
efficacy.quote: Setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. had no significant effect on this endpoint in the Phase 3 trial (−0.02 [95% CI −0.12, 0.07]; p = 0.652).
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (open access, PMC5379543). Neither field trial has posted registry results. Setipiprant was never run in the rhinitis chamber, so the class prediction comes from sibling members (BI 671800 in Krug 2014; QAV680 in a congress abstract).
efficacy.judgement: Contra because the chamber predicted class efficacy and the only adequately powered field Phase 3 of a member (95% power for a 0.20 DNSS difference) found nothing on the primary or any secondary endpoint, and development stopped. Ratner itself puts the chamber evidence beside its results ('in line with the growing clinical evidence from several CRHT2 antagonists investigated in allergen challenge trials'), so comparison_stated is true, but it draws that line only for the positive Phase 2 and calls the Phase 3 reasons 'not fully known', hence unresolved. The positive Phase 2 (NCT01241214, n=579, -0.15, p=0.030, no multiplicity correction) is the same-year 'same' that the Phase 3 contra outranks; a re-scorer who requires a same-drug chamber-vs-field pair would leave this untested. Dated to the paper: no 2012 sponsor announcement was found. Rulings 2026-11-09: year 2012 by rule 6 (Phase 3 miss public 2012-04-02 in Actelion's release via RTTNews, tier 5; earliest chamber result Horak 2012, OC000459, epub 2012-10-01, sibling model side). Efficacy is a target claim, so a chamber result first public after another CRTH2 antagonist's patient result is a retrodiction; it predicted benefit where the field showed none, so contra with retrodiction true.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: chamber TNSS AUC(0-6h) -17% vs placebo (BI 671800 200 mg b.i.d., p=0.0026) against field DNSS -0.02 (p=0.652) in Phase 3 and -0.15 (p=0.030) in Phase 2; the chamber gives no field effect-size prediction

patient_trials.quote: A statistically significant, dose-related improvement in mean change from baseline DNSS was observed over 2 weeks with setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. versus placebo in the Phase 2 trial (−0.15 [95% CI −0.29, −0.01]; p = 0.030).
Setipiprant dose-related efficacy in the Phase 2 trial was not confirmed during Phase 3.

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse allergic rhinitis (sneezing, nasal rubs, nasal obstruction)
efficacy.note: Selective DP2 antagonists relieved sneezing and nasal rubs in sensitised mice; only non-member class compounds were ever reported in it. Opens the setipiprant track (the only member scored against this model); the compounds dosed were siblings.
efficacy.short: DP2 antagonists work in mouse rhinitis
efficacy.quote: The lead compound was demonstrated to have efficacy in a mouse model of allergic rhinitis following oral dosing.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Members in this model: none found. Sandham 2013 reports QAV680 'efficacy in rodent CRTh2-dependent mechanistic and allergic disease models' without naming rhinitis in the abstract; the full text (ScienceDirect) returned 403, so whether QAV680 was run in a rhinitis model is unverified.
efficacy.judgement: Separate animal track, opened with a class proxy (product_in_model false): the Amira tricyclics here, AM156 (Stebbins 2010, doi 10.1016/j.ejphar.2010.04.031) and ARRY-063 (Shiraishi 2014, doi 10.1111/cea.12280). Setipiprant's discovery paper (Fretz 2013, doi 10.1021/jm400122f) reports in vitro potency and rat/dog PK only.

efficacy.model: OVA-sensitised mouse allergic rhinitis (sneezing, nasal rubs, nasal obstruction)
efficacy.note: Mouse said selective DP2 antagonism stops sneezing and nasal rubs; the class's one field Phase 3 (setipiprant) moved no nasal symptom. Dated 2012: Stebbins 2010 model side; Phase 3 miss public 2012-04-02 (Actelion release).
efficacy.short: Mouse nasal-symptom relief absent in Phase 3
efficacy.quote: In the Phase 3 trial, setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. was not associated with significant treatment differences versus placebo for any of the individual rDNSS symptom scores (Fig. 3 b).
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by me: no source puts the mouse model beside a member's field trial, and no member was ever reported in the model. Low confidence for that reason, not for the trial data (full text read).
efficacy.reason: Mouse-predicted class effect absent in Phase 3
efficacy.judgement: Allowed under v3 as a sibling-dosed model (product_in_model false) compared with a member's trial. The model side named is AM156 (Stebbins 2010), the explicit sneezing/nasal-rub result. Contra beats the Phase 2 'same' on the same track. A re-scorer who sets aside sibling-dosed animal evidence would leave this track untested. Rule 6: year 2012 (Actelion release 2012-04-02 via RTTNews, tier 5), not the 2017 paper; Stebbins 2010 predates it, so prospective.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse sneezing and nasal rubs inhibited (AM156) against field rDNSS items all non-significant in Phase 3; no common quantity

patient_trials.quote: Setipiprant dose-related efficacy in the Phase 2 trial was not confirmed during Phase 3.

efficacy.model: Bronchial allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (setipiprant proof-of-mechanism)
efficacy.note: Setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. cut the allergen-induced late asthmatic response by 25.6% in 15 asthmatics: the proof of mechanism behind the SAR field trials.
efficacy.quote: Compared with placebo, setipiprant significantly reduced the allergen-induced late asthmatic response (LAR), inhibiting the area under the response vs. time curve (AUC(3-10 h) ) by on average 25.6% (P = 0.006)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only (paywalled); quote is the verbatim opening of a longer sentence. Public record (2014) postdates the trials it dose-selected (2010-2012).
efficacy.judgement: This is the system setipiprant went into SAR patients on (Ratner 2017 calls it the proof-of-mechanism study behind the 1000 mg b.i.d. dose), so it is its own track; it predicts for the class via another indication's challenge, hence model_kind cross_indication.

efficacy.model: Bronchial allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (setipiprant proof-of-mechanism)
efficacy.note: Same drug, same regimen: positive Phase 2 (-0.15 DNSS) then null Phase 3 (miss public 2012-04-02). Challenge first public 2014, after the miss: a retrodiction that failed to reproduce it.
efficacy.quote: Setipiprant dose-related efficacy in the Phase 2 trial was not confirmed during Phase 3.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). No registry results for either trial.
efficacy.judgement: Contra on the primary (DNSS, fixed-sequence multiplicity control in Phase 3). Ratner states the comparison (dose chosen on the PoM) and leaves the discrepancy 'not fully known', so unresolved. Phase 2 was the same-year 'same' that the Phase 3 outranks. Rule 6: the comparison was public once both halves were, Diamant 2014 (2014-08-01) after the 2012-04-02 release, so year 2014. Post-dating alone makes it a retrodiction; it predicted benefit the Phase 3 did not show, so contra, retrodiction true. No earlier congress abstract of the challenge study was found.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: LAR AUC -25.6% in the challenge against field DNSS -0.02 (p=0.652) in Phase 3; no common quantity

patient_trials.quote: A statistically significant, dose-related improvement in mean change from baseline DNSS was observed over 2 weeks with setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. versus placebo in the Phase 2 trial (−0.15 [95% CI −0.29, −0.01]; p = 0.030).
Setipiprant 1000 mg b.i.d. had no significant effect on this endpoint in the Phase 3 trial (−0.02 [95% CI −0.12, 0.07]; p = 0.652).

safety.note: First member chamber study (QAV680, 10 days); chamber studies carry 2-week tolerability only.
safety.quote: This study will compare the effectiveness of QAV680 against placebo in treating the symptoms of seasonal allergic rhinitis in an Environmental Exposure Chamber.
safety.confidence_note: Registry record only; no results posted.
safety.judgement: Opens the chamber track in safety at the same point as the other cells.

safety.note: Chamber predicted no harm from 2 weeks of a CRTH2 antagonist (BI 671800); setipiprant's 2-week field trials saw AE rates below placebo.
safety.short: No harm predicted, none seen in field
safety.quote: Overall, setipiprant was well tolerated, and no safety issues were identified during either the Phase 2 or the Phase 3 trial.
safety.confidence_note: Paired by me across members (BI 671800 chamber, setipiprant field); a 2-week chamber study can only predict short-term tolerability, and Krug's safety statement is abstract-level ('had a favorable safety profile').
safety.judgement: Same, direction only, as the house style scores a challenge model's 'no harm' prediction that held. Three setipiprant Phase 3 patients had ALT/AST >3x ULN and one SAE (cholelithiasis, judged unrelated); Ratner identifies no safety issue, so this is not scored as a contradicted silence.
safety.magnitude_basis: no harm predicted, no harm seen; AE incidence 7.1-11.4% on setipiprant vs 13.5-16.3% on placebo, frequencies not compared with the chamber

safety.model: Bronchial allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (setipiprant proof-of-mechanism)
safety.note: The PoM study stated 1000 mg b.i.d. for 5 days was tolerated with no clinically relevant adverse events.
safety.quote: Overall, setipiprant was well tolerated and no clinically relevant adverse events occurred.
safety.judgement: Opens the asthma-challenge track in safety with the model's stated tolerability prediction for the regimen it chose.

safety.model: Bronchial allergen challenge in mild allergic asthmatics (setipiprant proof-of-mechanism)
safety.note: Same drug, same regimen: tolerated in the 5-day challenge, tolerated over 2 weeks in 1,209 field-trial participants.
safety.quote: Overall, setipiprant was well tolerated, and no safety issues were identified during either the Phase 2 or the Phase 3 trial.
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (open access). The comparison is stated: Ratner cites the PoM as having shown the dose 'was well tolerated' and reports the same for both field trials.
safety.reason: Tolerability held, same drug and dose
safety.judgement: Same, direction only: the model stated no harm at the regimen and none appeared. Headache (Phase 1) and dry mouth (field) are the only recurring AEs; neither is a model-predicted harm. This is the same-drug tolerability pairing; the chamber track above is the cross-member one.
safety.magnitude_basis: no harm predicted at 1000 mg b.i.d., none seen; AE incidence 7.1-11.4% on setipiprant vs 13.5-16.3% on placebo
